confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from web search summaries of aggregated cost-of-living sites (Numbeo, world-prices, theworldtravelindex) and 2026 Havana budget and bar guides. These sources disagree quite a lot. The cappuccino estimates ran from about $1.11 to $3, and inexpensive meals from about $5 to $11. They also quote prices in different currencies (USD, CUP and the retired CUC), and Cuba's official and informal CUP rates differ widely, so tourist-facing prices may not match the crowd-sourced data. For the mid-range meal for two, the sources put the figure at about $20 to $27.50 (Numbeo's range was $16.80 to $50). I chose $34 to reflect tourist-facing paladares. Beer is set at about $2.20, the most common figure across sources for a local draft beer or a Cristal/Bucanero. Cocktails are based on reported mojito prices of about $5 to $9 in central tourist bars, with lower happy-hour prices. Wine evidence was weak: one news item gave a high-end restaurant price in CUP that only converts roughly at an informal rate. So I estimated wine from its local price relationship to beer and cocktails, and the wine figure is the least certain of the drink anchors. Accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates and were not searched or checked against listings. Much budget lodging in Havana is in casas particulares rather than registered hostels. Three-star rooms in state-run hotels vary a lot, and occupancy has dropped during Cuba's economic crisis.
comparable_city_reasoning: Havana is based on its own aggregated 2026 price data, adjusted for tourist-facing private restaurants (paladares) and bars. For accommodation, I used Havana's casa particular and state-hotel market and compared it with lower-cost Caribbean and Central American capitals such as Santo Domingo and Managua.
